'''Sir David Allan''' "'''Dai'''" '''Rees''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lawson |first1=Chris |last2=Lillford |first2=Peter |date=2023 |title=Sir David Allan (Dai) Rees. 28 April 1936—10 June 2021 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=74|pages=387–402 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2022.0043 |s2cid=256416921 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (28 April 1936 – 10 June 2021)<ref name=debretts>{{cite web|url=http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/r/4701/David%20Allan%20%28Dai%29+REES.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231000603/http://www.debretts.com/people/biographies/browse/r/4701/David%20Allan%20(Dai)+REES.aspx |archive-date=31 December 2013 |title=Sir Dai Rees, FRS|website=[[Debrett's People of Today]]|accessdate=28 December 2013}}</ref> was a British [[biochemist]] and science administrator who was chief executive of the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] between 1987 and 1996.<ref name=whoswho/>

==Early life and education==
Rees was born in [[Silloth]], [[Cumberland]]<ref name=debretts/> and educated in Wales: he attended [[Hawarden High School|Hawarden Grammar School]]<ref name=whoswho/><ref name=le>{{cite news|url=http://www.le.ac.uk/bulletin/bulletinapr97.pdf|title=Honorary degrees at Leicester University|newspaper=[[Leicester University]] Bulletin|date=April 1997|page=18|access-date=28 December 2013|archive-date=18 April 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070418032014/http://www.le.ac.uk/bulletin/bulletinapr97.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and received his BSc and PhD degrees in chemistry from [[University College of North Wales, Bangor]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-24707045.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140610193601/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-24707045.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=10 June 2014|title=Sir Dai Rees|date=13 October 2003|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]}}</ref>

==Career==
Rees was a lecturer in chemistry at the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 1960 until 1970, researching [[carbohydrate conformation]] and structure.<ref name=colworth/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/sir-dai-rees/|title=Sir Dai Rees FRS FMedSci FLSW|work=Fellows directory|publisher=[[Academy of Medical Sciences]]|access-date=28 December 2013|archive-date=30 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230234715/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/sir-dai-rees/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He then joined [[Unilever]], where he rose to become principal scientist. He left in 1982 to become director of the [[National Institute for Medical Research]], and then was chief executive of the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] from 1987 to 1996. He was president of the [[European Science Foundation]] from 1994 to1999.<ref name=debretts/>

==Honours and awards==
Rees received a [[Doctor of Science#United Kingdom, Ireland, India, Pakistan and the Commonwealth|DSc]] degree from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1969.<ref>{{cite book | title=Polysaccharide structure, shape, and function | publisher=WorldCat
| oclc=1064002735}}</ref> In 1970, Rees was awarded both the Carbohydrate Chemistry Award by the [[Chemical Society]] and the [[Colworth Medal]] by the [[Biochemical Society]].<ref name=colworth>{{cite journal|title=Shapely polysaccharides: The eighth Colworth Medal Lecture|first=DA|last=Rees|journal=[[Biochemical Journal]]|volume=126|issue=2|pages=257–273|pmc=1178377|year=1972|pmid=4561024|doi=10.1042/bj1260257}}</ref> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1981|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1981]] and delivered the Royal Society's [[Philips Lecture]] in 1984. He was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[1993 Birthday Honours]].<ref name=debretts/> He was an inaugural [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (1998).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Deceased Fellows |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/more-fellowship/deceased-fellows |access-date=2026-06-12 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref> He was one of the 58 founding fellows of the [[Learned Society of Wales]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://learnedsocietywales.ac.uk/node/13|title=Founding Fellows|publisher=The [[Learned Society of Wales]]|access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref>
